name: Loango National Park
subtitle: A coastal park in Gabon where forest elephants, buffalo and hippos walk out onto the beach.

parts.text: Loango National Park lies in western Gabon, between the Nkomi and Ndogo lagoons, and covers 1,550 square kilometres. It was established in 2002.
It protects savanna, beach, forest and mangrove, including part of the 220 km² Iguéla Lagoon, and more than 100 kilometres of uninhabited coastline.
Conservation reporters call it a pristine forest-savanna mosaic.

Elephants, buffalo, hippopotamuses, gorillas and leopards live on land, and humpback and killer whales in the sea. The park is known for elephants, buffalo, hippos, gorillas and leopards going out onto the beaches.

Gabon set aside 13 national parks, more than 10,000 square miles and about 10% of the country. The Wildlife Conservation Society had done field research in Gabon since 1985 and helped plan the parks through surveys of remote areas.
The Mongabay report is dated September 2005 and speaks of the parks as announced then; Wikipedia gives 2002 for Loango's establishment. The sources do not agree on the timeline.
Conservationists in the report describe resolving conflicts between loggers and preservationists, with the scientist Lee White steering logging away from the most sensitive areas.

gaps: When the parks were created. The two sources read give 2002 (for Loango) and September 2005 (for the announcement of the 13 parks); neither is an official Gabonese document.
The state of the park and its animals today. No count of elephants or other wildlife was read, and the sources are a 2005 news report and Wikipedia.
Who lives around the park and how it affects them. The sources read are written from the conservation side.
Whether and how it can be visited, which lodges operate there and what they cost. Nothing about access was read.
The coordinates are Wikipedia's for the park as a whole, not an entrance.
